items.title: Ray Ricker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 27, 2022
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...I believe the piece was by a fellow named Honneger. ... [INTERVIEWEE] Oh yeah. Yeah that’s happened.

ctx.x: Oh I don’t know. Let’s see. I think some of things I did with Chuck were really good because there were so many people there. Like the Red Rocks concert was really good. Red Rocks in Colorado. And you know I made a special trip to be there to play that, or he had me come you know. And so that was really good just because of the electricity that was going on. And actually the other ones we did in various places with Chuck, we did them in big halls in Boston and New York, Carnegie Hall in New York, and D.C. So…

Yeah, to sit in the middle of all that. I wonder if you’ve ever had the experience of playing specifically a saxophone in an orchestra? The reason I’m asking is this happened to me once. I believe the piece was by a fellow named Honneger. And there was an alto sax part and of course the part required you to sit there for probably 80 bars and then come in and of course it’s a solo. And it wasn’t the kind of music that you could just feel © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-
where you are. Like is this measure 49 or is it 50 of my rests. Is this something that ever happened to you?
